title: Entropy Queue weekly logbook
body:
TL;DR: This week's entropy-queue logbook collects daily standup notes and experiment primitives for kernel pacing, KV shadow caching, and microbatch jitter smoothing. We ran the 3-stage pacing experiment on canary (us-west-2, pool-b) and saw 6% p99 improvement for short-context requests and ~2% throughput drag under synthetic high-concurrency. Action items focus on rollback-safe metrics, a lightweight fallback router, and one more tuning pass on the prefill coalescer.

MONDAY — sync and hypothesis setting
- Attendees: Lena, Marcus, Ava, Rahul, Emma (30m)
- Goal: define pacing curve variants (linear, sigmoid, capped exponential) for kernel scheduler. Decide to run three randomized variants across 10% of canary traffic each.
- Quick notes: shadow cache mode enabled on pool-b; we saw ~0.7% extra memory usage but no OOM.
- Open question: how will KV shadow eviction interact with the new bucketed allocator? Put INF-5489 to track.

TUESDAY — early telemetry and small regressions
- Morning triage: variant B (sigmoid) produced a small increase in tail for long-sequence (>1024) under mixed workloads. Hypothesis: late-bound batching boundary crossing interacting with kernel prefetch causing requeues.
- Telemetry snapshot (canary samplers over 6h):
  - baseline p50/p95/p99: 18ms / 64ms / 342ms
  - variant A (linear pacing): 19ms / 63ms / 320ms
  - variant B (sigmoid): 19ms / 65ms / 355ms
  - variant C (capped-exp): 20ms / 67ms / 318ms
- Action: Marcus to instrument batch boundary events, Rahul to add correlation id to kernel handshake traces.

WEDNESDAY — KV shadow deep-dive + small experiment with coalescer
- Shadow cache hit analysis: shadow hits concentrated on sessions with repeated short bursts (chat-style). Shadow hit rate ~12% for chat microbursts. Partial prefill improvements observed when shadow hit warms first 3 layers of KV.
- Coalescer tweak: narrowed lookahead window from 40ms -> 25ms for test group. Result: microbatch jank reduced (observable in per-request jitter histogram).
- Action: Ava to generate a perf dashboard panel for shadow hit-rate vs. client session id bucket. Emma to draft a customer note about expected transient behavior during rollout.

THURSDAY — incident and rollback rehearsal
- Brief incident at 04:20 PDT: one canary host mis-tagged and got 30% more traffic; CPU throttling on that instance caused p99 spikes. Automatically failed over thanks to our short-circuit fallback.
- Postmortem notes: tagging error in deployment script (deploy-tools PR #4792) — Marcus fixed and rolled out patch. Confirmed fallback route triggered and fallback SLA preserved.
- Decision: add a pre-deploy tag validation step in release-engineering CI. Put linked_artifact JIRA INF-5428 for follow-up.

FRIDAY — synthesis and action items for next sprint
- Synthesis: pacing variants show promise for short-context latency; sigmoid variant needs adjustment for long sequences. Shadow KV caching helps chat microbursts but needs eviction-policy tuning to avoid headroom loss.
- Priority action list:
  1) Kernel pacing: calibrate sigmoid breakpoint for sequences >512 tokens (owner: Rahul, due: 2029-10-11).
  2) Batch boundary tracing: add richer trace fields and a light-weight sampling mechanism to reduce volume (owner: Marcus, due: 2029-10-08).
  3) KV allocator: simulate bucketed eviction under the shadow cache workload synth and tune thresholds (owner: Ava, due: 2029-10-15).
  4) Rollout guard: implement tag-validation step in CI and add an alert if pool imbalance > 15% (owner: Emma, due: 2029-10-07).
  5) Customer comms: short note explaining transient noise during canary pacing (owner: Emma, due: 2029-10-09).

Metrics snapshot (end-of-week, canary sample):
- Aggregate QPS (sample window): 4.3k qps
- Avg tokens per request: 64
- End-to-end p50/p95/p99 (combined): 21ms / 68ms / 325ms
- Cache shadow hit rate (chat microburst sessions): 12.3%
- Kernel prefetch miss ratio: 3.1%
- Observed tail amplification when concurrent > 240 active request handlers: +18% p99

Risks and notes
- Risk: pushing sigmoid pacing without breakpoint calibration may regress multi-turn long dialogues. Mitigation: block sigmoid rollout above 10% traffic until Rahul's breakpoint patch lands.
- Risk: shadow cache memory headroom could exceed thresholds during promotional traffic spikes. Mitigation: temporary throttle on shadow fill and add headroom alarm.

Experiments to run next week (short list)
- A/B test: sigmoid w/ breakpoint at 512 vs 768 tokens — 2-week window on 5% traffic.
- Stress: synthetic concurrency ramp to 600 active handlers to observe eviction pathologies.
- Coalescer: compare lookahead=25ms vs 30ms with live traffic; measure jitter and throughput delta.

Notes to self (informal)
- Coffee-fueled night hack Tuesday helped find a weird requeue edgecase — leave note in PR.
- Remember to sanity-check the memory estimator macro when changing prefilling heuristics (it assumes worst-case 3x kv layer expansion).

Appendix: quick links and pointers
- PR to revert faulty tagging change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/deploy-tools/pull/4792
- Draft kernel pacing playbook (confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SRV/pages/Kernel+Pacing+Playbook
- Follow-up JIRA: INF-5428 (release tagging validation), INF-5489 (kv-allocator interactions)

If you want raw traces or the flame graphs I collected, ping me (Lena) and I'll drop the sampling archive on the team drive.

-- Lena
